channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Novo tarifaço dos EUA reforça discurso eleitoral de Lula respaldado por pesquisas
item.description: The new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods bolster Lula’s electoral narrative of defending national sovereignty, with polls showing public support. The PT campaign attributes the decision to the Bolsonaro clan while preparing economic measures to mitigate impacts. The government’s response will split between political messaging and pending commercial retaliation.

item.title: Convenções partidárias começam em 20 de julho; confira as datas e as regras
item.description: Party conventions for the 2026 elections will take place between July 20 and August 5, defining candidacies and coalitions for majoritarian and proportional offices. The first pre-candidate to hold a convention will be Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) on July 25, followed by Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) on July 26, Romeu Zema (Novo) on July 27, Renan Santos (Mission) on August 1, and Lula on August 2, all in in-person, virtual, or hybrid formats as permitted by party statutes.

item.title: Criado o Dia Nacional da Capoeira, a ser celebrado em 15 de julho
item.description: National Capoeira Day was established to be celebrated on July 15 under Law 15.469, sanctioned by the Presidency of the Republic. The date commemorates the recognition of capoeira as Brazil’s Intangible Cultural Heritage and highlights its role as a cultural resistance practice rooted in the struggles of enslaved Africans, reinforcing national identity and regional diversity.

item.title: Governo rejeita críticas e diz que fez mais de 30 contatos com os EUA para negociar tarifas
item.description: The Brazilian government rejects criticism over the new U.S. tariff, stating it has made over 30 contacts since the original announcement to negotiate a solution, including meetings with Marco Rubio and Jamieson Greer. The measure, set to take effect on July 22, was labeled 'lamentable' by the government, which vows to invoke the reciprocity law. The opposition blames Lula for negotiation failures, while the government attributes the U.S. decision to ideological and political motives.

item.title: Tarifaço: aliado de Flávio vê 'militância ideológica' do governo, que reage ao clã Bolsonaro e cita 'falsos patriotas'
item.description: Allies of pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) accused the Lula government of causing the U.S. tariff hike through an ideologically driven foreign policy that ignored negotiations with Washington and reacted late to trade barriers from China and the EU. Senator Rogério Marinho said the government 'reaps what it sows', while Marcelo Freixo accused Flávio and the Bolsonaro clan of conspiring for electoral gain, labeling them 'false patriots'. The federal government called July 15 a 'lamentable milestone' in Brazil-U.S. relations and pledged to activate reciprocal measures under the Reciprocity Law.

item.title: Nikolas Ferreira ironiza governo Lula após tarifa de 25%: "Make the L"
item.description: Federal Deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-RJ) mocked President Lula's government after the U.S. announced a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, using the phrase 'Make the L' in reference to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who blamed Lula for lacking good faith in negotiations. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) also attacked the government, claiming Lula is leaving the country 'on a plane without a pilot' and accusing him of corruption, incompetence, and vengeance, despite initially advocating for delaying the tariffs until after the 2026 elections.

item.title: O novo gesto de Flávio para tentar ganhar terreno sobre eleitorado feminino
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL's pre-candidate for president, will launch the 'Brazil for Her' plan in a live stream to appeal to female voters, following a public rift with Michelle Bolsonaro and declining support among women. The announcement will feature Daniella Marques, former aide to Paulo Guedes and a potential running mate. The plan, developed after meetings with female PL leaders, aims to regain ground lost with female electorate.

item.title: EE UU impone nuevos aranceles del 25% a gran parte de productos brasileños y acusa a Lula de no negociar “de buena fe”
item.description: The United States has imposed a new 25% tariff on most Brazilian products, accusing Brazil of unfair competition. The Lula administration labeled the move as purely political and announced it will activate the Reciprocity Law to apply equivalent measures on U.S. goods. This tariff escalation is expected to become a central issue in the 2026 Brazilian elections, where Lula will face Flávio Bolsonaro, as a similar move in 2025 had previously boosted the president’s popularity.

item.title: Vídeo: Davi anuncia duas semanas de esforço concentrado após o recesso
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre announced the dates for the concentrated effort to vote on bills during the electoral period: August 10–14 and August 31–September 3. The work will be coordinated with the Chamber of Deputies’ concentrated efforts, as agreed with Chamber President Deputy Hugo Motta.

item.title: Lula usa tarifaço dos EUA para carimbar Flávio como ‘traidor’ e estratégia vira mote da campanha
item.description: President Lula will use the U.S. decision to impose a 25% tariff on Brazilian products to attack Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, accusing him of betraying the nation in collaboration with the Trump government. Lula's re-election campaign will intensify the 'Tariflávio' slogan on social media and in radio and TV ads starting in August, linking Flávio to actions against national interests, including the Master scandal. The Presidency's Secom issued a note blaming the tariff on the Bolsonaro family, claiming they acted for electoral motives, not love for Brazil.

item.title: Tarifaço: Flávio diz que Lula provocou Trump “o tempo inteiro”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) accused President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of repeatedly provoking former U.S. President Donald Trump over 62 times, which he claims led to the U.S. imposing a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods effective July 22. The Lula administration denied the allegations, calling the tariff part of a 'plot actively collaborated on by the Bolsonaro family' and emphasized that defending national sovereignty is a non-partisan duty. Brazil is also awaiting a second investigation that could add a 12.5% tariff, potentially raising total duties to 37.5% in certain sectors.

item.title: Líderes do PL dizem que Lula quer usar tarifas como "arma eleitoral"
item.description: PL leaders, including Sóstenes Cavalcante and Rogério Marinho, accuse President Lula of using the 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods as an 'electoral weapon', claiming the Lula government is responsible due to alleged bad-faith negotiations with the United States. They argue Lula 'reaps what he sows' by turning foreign policy into ideological militancy, neglecting dialogue with Washington. The opposition also mocks the PT as the 'Tariff Party'.

item.title: A expectativa do Itamaraty sobre a retomada das negociações do tarifaço com os EUA
item.description: Despite the confirmation of 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, Itamaraty states that the Lula government will keep diplomatic channels open, though without expecting a shift in Washington’s stance. The move is seen as politically motivated, tied to Trump’s July 9 post demanding an end to Bolsonaro’s STF trial, with Brazil having held over 30 contacts across presidential, ministerial, and technical levels. The government disputes the USTR investigation’s basis, citing a 50% reduction in Amazon deforestation from 2022 to 2025 and denying any proposal to restrict Pix.

item.title: Lula está ranzinza e se tornou perigo para o Brasil, diz Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro harshly criticized President Lula, calling him the 'Brazilian Biden' and saying he is 'grumpy, inconsistent, and has become a danger' to Brazil, in response to comments by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and the new 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian exports.

item.title: Governo Trump aponta ‘culpado’ pelo tarifaço contra o Brasil
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio blamed President Lula and the Brazilian government for the 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, accusing them of failing to negotiate in good faith and prioritizing ego over national interest. Brazil’s Itamaraty countered that it initiated over 30 contacts with U.S. officials — including 11 with Rubio and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer — but received no counterproposals from the American side.

item.title: Quaest indica que novo tarifaço é pior para Flávio do que para Lula
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows that the new U.S. 25% tariff on about 3,000 Brazilian products has a more negative political impact on Senator Flávio Bolsonaro than on President Lula. Lula accused Flávio of lobbying Trump for the tariff, which the senator denies. The findings suggest greater electoral vulnerability for Flávio Bolsonaro ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Governo Lula classifica decisão dos EUA como 'ideológica' e diz que equipe de Trump agiu de má-fé
item.description: The Lula government labeled the U.S. decision to impose 25% tariffs on Brazilian products as ideological and made in bad faith, claiming it aims to benefit Flávio Bolsonaro. Brazil states the decision was made since last year and will immediately initiate procedures to invoke the Economic Reciprocity Law.

item.title: Vídeo: Davi anuncia calendário de esforço concentrado em agosto e setembro
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre announced that Congress will hold two weeks of concentrated effort: from August 10–14 and August 31–September 3, 2024. The decision, made jointly with the Chamber of Deputies, aims to align the legislative calendar with the municipal electoral period, allowing lawmakers to engage in campaigns while maintaining institutional functioning.

item.title: O que é a Lei da Reciprocidade, que Brasil disse que usará contra EUA
item.description: The Brazilian government announced it will invoke the Economic Reciprocity Law against the U.S. in response to a new 25% tariff on Brazilian exports, justified by claims of favoring Pix, ethanol market access, corruption, and deforestation. The law, passed in April 2025 and regulated by decree in July 2024, allows proportional countermeasures such as suspending trade concessions and intellectual property obligations when unilateral actions harm Brazil’s international competitiveness. The government labeled the U.S. measure a 'regrettable milestone' and will pursue resolution through the WTO.

item.title: Neymar joga contra o Botafogo? Entenda situação do camisa 10 para duelo com o Santos
item.description: Neymar will not play against Botafogo this Thursday, as he is on vacation following Brazil's elimination from the 2026 World Cup. He is set to return to Santos training on Friday, one day after the match. His contract with the club ends at the season's conclusion, though there is an expectation he will fulfill it through December.

item.title: Áudio: Aprovada prorrogação de autorização de uso do FGTS para crédito a hospitais
item.description: The Senate approved extending until the end of 2030 the authorization to use FGTS funds for credit lines to philanthropic hospitals and nonprofit institutions operating within the SUS, such as Santa Casas. Bill 2.465/2026 now proceeds to presidential sanction.

item.title: As intenções de voto para presidente entre os eleitores de Rondônia, segundo nova pesquisa
item.description: In Rondônia, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leads presidential voting intentions with 58% in the first round, followed by Lula (PT) at 25%. In a hypothetical runoff, Bolsonaro’s lead over Lula widens to 42 points (66% to 24%). The survey, conducted by Real Time Big Data between July 14–15, interviewed 1,600 voters with a margin of error of two percentage points.

item.title: Planalto culpa ‘família Bolsonaro’ por tarifaço do governo Trump: ‘São falsos patriotas’
item.description: The Brazilian government blamed the Bolsonaro family for the 25% tariff imposed by the United States on Brazilian products, claiming that Jair Bolsonaro's sons actively collaborated in the U.S. to advance electoral interests. The Presidency labeled them 'false patriots' and announced Brazil will respond with reciprocal tariffs and pursue the dispute through the WTO and the Reciprocity Law.

item.title: Flávio volta a criticar Lula ao comentar post de Rubio que indica tarifaço como ato político
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a pre-candidate for president in 2026, harshly criticized President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) after the U.S. announced a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, blaming Lula for the measure due to alleged bad-faith negotiations. He compared Lula to Joe Biden, calling him 'inconsequential' and a 'danger to the nation,' and stated that Brazil 'has no more time to lose.' The remarks came in response to a post by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who also accused Lula of harming bilateral interests, although the USTR denied the tariff was politically motivated.

item.title: Diplomacia brasileira teve mais de 30 contatos com governo Trump para tentar evitar tarifaço
item.description: Brazilian diplomacy conducted over 30 contacts with the Trump administration to avoid a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, including 11 meetings with Secretary of State Marco Rubio and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer. Despite these efforts, the U.S. imposed the tariffs, which Brazil denounced as a politically motivated retaliation tied to the trial of former President Bolsonaro before the STF. Brazil invoked its reciprocity law and blamed the Bolsonaro family for collaborating with U.S. investigations that led to the measure.

item.title: Flávio paga o preço de crises em massacre de números
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential pre-candidacy collapsed, with 42% of voters siding with his stepmother Michelle Bolsonaro's accusations against him, versus only 18% who support him, per Genial/Quaest poll. 54% of Brazilians view him as an extremist like his father and brothers, while 69% back ending the 6×1 work schedule, further isolating the Bolsonaro clan. His frantic social media attempt to discredit the poll was seen as a sign of desperation.

item.title: Rejeição eleitoral a Flávio Bolsonaro aumenta e chega a 57%
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's electoral rejection rose to 57% in June, according to Quaest/Genial, up five points from April. His declining vote intentions are tied to scandals involving funds from a jailed bank owner accused of billion-dollar fraud and a public feud with former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro. While Lula holds steady at 40% support, Bolsonaro risks exceeding 60% rejection by the first round.

item.title: Os cenários da disputa pela presidência no segundo turno, segundo a nova pesquisa Poder/Aya
item.description: Lula leads all second-round scenarios in the Poder/Aya poll, but only holds a clear advantage over Renan Santos (Missão). He is in a technical tie with Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Romeu Zema (Novo), and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), with margins within the two-point margin of error. The survey interviewed 2,400 people via phone between July 12 and 15, 2026.

item.title: Lula lidera a disputa em primeiro turno, mostra pesquisa Poder/Aya
item.description: Lula leads the 2026 presidential race with 40% voting intention, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro with 34%, according to the Poder/Aya poll released on July 16, 2026. The incumbent president holds a six-point lead over his main rival, while other pre-candidates remain below 10%. The survey interviewed 2,400 people by phone between July 12 and 15, with a margin of error of two percentage points.

item.title: Assaí diz que abrirá 25 farmácias no Estado de São Paulo
item.description: Assaí announced the launch of Assaí Farma, its own pharmacy operation, with the first unit opening at the Anhanguera store in São Paulo on July 16, 2026. The company plans to open 25 pharmacies in São Paulo state during the second half of 2026, with sales also available via the Meu Assaí app. The initiative is enabled by Law 15.357/2026, signed by President Lula in March 2026, which permits pharmacies to operate inside supermarkets.

item.title: Flávio responsabiliza Lula por tarifas: "Estamos num avião sem piloto"
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a pre-candidate for president in 2026, blamed President Lula for the 25% tariffs imposed by the U.S. on Brazilian goods, stating Brazil is 'an airplane without a pilot'. He compared Lula to Joe Biden, calling the petista 'grumpy, inconsistent, and a danger to the nation', and said 'whoever sees Lula sees no future'.

item.title: Flávio culpa Lula por tarifaço e chama petista de “Biden brasileiro”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) accused President Lula (PT) of being responsible for the decision by the Donald Trump government to impose a 25% tariff on most Brazilian imports. He also stated that Lula 'no longer has the conditions to be president of Brazil' and called him the 'Brazilian Biden'.

item.title: Governo federal vai lançar campanha sobre danos causados por bets
item.description: The Ministry of Health is preparing a public awareness campaign about the harms of online betting, focusing on mental health risks, identifying problematic use, and promoting SUS support services. The campaign required TSE authorization due to the electoral blackout period, which was granted by court president Nunes Marques. Set to launch in July and run through October, it functions as a public health prevention measure to expand access to care and reduce stigma.

item.title: 42% dizem que apoio de Trump é negativo para candidato a presidente
item.description: A PoderData/Aya poll shows 42% of Brazilian voters view a potential endorsement by Donald Trump for a presidential candidate as negative, 32% as positive, and 20% as neutral. The finding comes amid rising trade tensions after the U.S. imposed 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods, which has become a central electoral issue, with Lula leveraging the episode to criticize Flávio Bolsonaro for seeking Trump’s support.

item.title: Lula e Flávio têm 48% de rejeição cada um, diz PoderData/Aya
item.description: The PoderData/Aya poll reveals that 48% of voters would 'never vote' for either Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro, showing equal rejection levels for the two main presidential pre-candidates in 2026. While 36% say they would vote only for Lula and 11% could consider him, Flávio has 30% definite support and 15% potential vote, with a slight numerical decline in his numbers compared to the June survey.

item.title: Lula tem 40% e Flávio, 34%, no 1º turno, diz PoderData/Aya
item.description: A PoderData/Aya poll shows President Lula leading with 40% of voting intentions, widening his gap over Flávio Bolsonaro, who holds 34%. Following Joaquim Barbosa's likely withdrawal, Renan Santos saw a slight increase in support, while other candidates remain within a technical tie.

item.title: ‘Vi há mais de um mês’, diz Valdemar sobre foto de Flávio Bolsonaro com ‘Sicário’ de Vorcaro
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL, said he had known for over a month about the photo of Flávio Bolsonaro alongside Luiz Phillipi Machado de Moraes Mourão, known as 'Sicário', who was killed in March and identified by the Federal Police as a member of the group 'A Turma', linked to banker Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: Governo Lula reage e diz que vai recorrer à OMC contra tarifaço
item.description: The Lula government announced it will invoke the Economic Reciprocity Law and file a complaint with the World Trade Organization (WTO) against the 25% tariff imposed by the United States on most Brazilian imports. The decision was communicated in a statement released early Thursday morning, January 16, in response to the Trump administration's trade measure.

item.title: Marco Rubio joga a culpa do tarifaço de Trump no colo de Lula
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio blamed Brazilian President Lula for the Trump administration's decision to impose a 25% tariff on certain Brazilian imports, claiming Trump made the decision after actions by the Brazilian government. The statement was made in a social media post and attributed to O Antagonista.

item.title: Quaest: Tarifaço pesa mais contra Flávio Bolsonaro do que contra Lula
item.description: The Quaest poll reveals that 51% of Brazilians believe Flávio Bolsonaro is responsible for the U.S. tariffs on Brazil, having allegedly urged Trump to impose sanctions, compared to 30% who accept his claim that he tried to prevent the taxation. Blame attributed to Flávio has risen since June (from 35% support for his defense to 30%), while Lula’s version gained traction (from 47% to 51%). Despite Flávio’s trip to the U.S., 57% of Brazilians were unaware of it.

item.title: 'Aprofundamento da ruptura antes das eleições' e 'altos riscos': como a imprensa internacional noticiou tarifa de 25% dos EUA contra o Brasil
item.description: International press, notably the Financial Times, highlighted that the U.S. decision to impose 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods reflects a deepening bilateral rupture ahead of Brazil’s October elections. The measure, justified by alleged unfair practices in sectors like Pix, ethanol, and intellectual property, was seen by Lula’s allies as potential electoral interference, especially following the U.S. designation of Brazilian criminal groups as terrorist organizations.

item.title: Aldo mantém pré-candidatura e leva disputa do DC à Justiça
item.description: Former minister Aldo Rebelo (DC) maintains his presidential pre-candidacy and asserts that the internal party dispute over the nominee will be resolved by the courts and the national convention, scheduled for July 20 to August 5, 2026. He was expelled from the DC after challenging the selection of Joaquim Barbosa as the party's pre-candidate, but a Federal District court suspended the expulsion, allowing him to remain affiliated. Rebelo criticizes political polarization and questions Barbosa's commitment to the candidacy, citing low polling numbers.

item.title: Nunes Marques manda excluir vídeo de influenciador petista com desinformação contra Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: TSE President Nunes Marques ordered the removal of a video by influencer Thiago dos Reis, a PT pre-candidate for federal deputy, which spread disinformation linking Flávio Bolsonaro to the PCC. The minister emphasized there is no indictment or accusation against the senator and cited the influencer’s history of misinformation to justify the risk of repetition.

item.title: Lula fez escolha política ao apoiar agricultura familiar, diz ministra
item.description: Minister of Agrarian Development and Family Agriculture Fernanda Machiaveli stated that the Lula government made a political choice to prioritize family farming, ensuring continued investment despite potential fiscal constraints. The 2026/2027 Harvest Plan allocated R$ 97.3 billion to family farming, with R$ 85.2 billion going to Pronaf, aiming to expand credit access for women, Indigenous, quilombola, settled, and rural youth producers, while boosting domestic food production.

item.title: Moraes assume a presidência do STF até o fim de julho
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes will assume the presidency of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) starting this Thursday (July 16, 2026) until July 31, during the mid-year judicial recess. As vice-president, he replaces President Luiz Edson Fachin, who led the judicial duty from July 2 to 15. Moraes previously held this role in January, when he ordered an investigation into a leak of ministers’ confidential data involving the Federal Revenue and Coaf, and is currently the rapporteur of Operation Exfil, which investigates the sale of sensitive information from officials and their families.

item.title: Governo redesenhou linhas do Pronaf para ampliar acesso, diz ministra
item.description: The Lula government redesigned Pronaf credit lines to expand access for family farmers, particularly in the Northeast and North, benefiting agrarian reform settlers, quilombolas, indigenous peoples, women, and youth. The 2026/2027 Harvest Plan allocated R$ 97.3 billion to family farming, with R$ 85.2 billion for Pronaf, resulting in over 2 million credit operations per harvest and stimulating production of staple foods.

item.title: Setor empresarial lamenta novo tarifaço de 25%, e Fiesp dispara contra governo Lula
item.description: Brazilian business leaders expressed concern and criticism over the new 25% tariff imposed by the U.S. government on Brazilian goods, with FIESP leading the backlash and accusing the Lula administration of failing to respond effectively. The measure, announced by Donald Trump, has raised alarms among São Paulo industrialists about the competitiveness of national industry.

item.title: O novo mote da campanha de Caiado
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado's campaign has introduced a new slogan to try to reverse its poor polling performance, where it stands at just 4% voting intention according to yesterday's Quaest survey. The strategy aims to move the candidate out of the electoral rut he currently finds himself in, though the specifics of the new motto were not disclosed in the available excerpt. The content is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: 'Olho por olho, dente por dente?' O que diz a Lei de Reciprocidade que Lula quer usar contra novo tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: President Lula plans to invoke the Economic Reciprocity Law, enacted in July 2025, to retaliate against the 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, citing alleged unfair practices such as Pix favoring, ethanol market access, corruption, and deforestation. The law allows Brazil to suspend trade concessions, investments, and intellectual property obligations in response to unilateral actions harming its international competitiveness. The government says it will pursue action through the WTO after rejecting the U.S. decision.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio criam memes com foto ao lado de Sicário
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro, including his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro and other PL deputies, shared AI-generated memes to defend him after controversy arose over a photo with Luiz Philipi Mourão, known as Sicário. The images depict Flávio alongside celebrities and fictional characters, reinforcing his claim that posing with someone does not imply a relationship. He also countered by sharing photos of Lula with Deolane Bezerra to draw a parallel.
